generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential integers starting at 1, unique per table; never NULL.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: Uniformly sample an existing parent key from the final surviving parent key set (compact + generated, after dedup); never NULL for NOT NULL FK columns; ~5% NULL only if the column is nullable; ensure at least one parent row has no children.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_text: Random string of length 4-12 drawn from lowercase letters plus space and digits; 20-50% duplicate share for DISTINCT-targeted columns; near-variants (case/whitespace/one-char edits) of listed equality literals; 0.3 of text values fresh, 0.7 drawn from observed pool.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_short_enum: Uniform choice from the table's enum list; case variants (lower/upper) allowed only where listed.
generic_sampling_rules.datetime: Random timestamp between 1970-01-01 and 2015-12-31 23:59:59 in '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'; boundary values at each listed literal and one day on each side planted with probability 0.35 per instance.
generic_sampling_rules.nullable_columns: Every nullable column receives NULL treatment: k = clamp(round(n*share), 1, n-1) so at least one NULL and at least one non-NULL generated row always exist; a compact share of 1.0 does not force all-NULL.
generic_sampling_rules.boundary_numbers: For each numeric literal L in targets, include L-1, L, L+1 with probability 0.35 per instance.
generic_sampling_rules.boundary_dates: For each date literal D, include D-1 day, D, D+1 day in the column format with probability 0.35 per instance.
generic_sampling_rules.tie_ranks: For ORDER-targeted aggregate columns, plant at least two parent rows sharing the rank-1 aggregate value (tie_rank read from per_column_exceptions).
generic_sampling_rules.fresh_value_share: 0.3 of text values are fresh (not from the observed pool); 0.7 drawn from observed pool.

supporting_evidence.Orders.order_status: Observed values Shipped, Packing, On Road in Orders.order_status sample.
supporting_evidence.Order_Items.order_item_status: Observed values Finish, Payed, Cancel in Order_Items.order_item_status sample.
supporting_evidence.date_bounds: All observed dates in Orders, Invoices, Shipments fall within 1970-01-01..2015-12-31 (e.g. Orders 1974-06-24, Invoices 1971-02-12, Shipments 1977-11-10).

generation_specification.uncertainty: The shipment_date >= order_date rule is contradicted by compact row shipment_id=1 (1983-08-13) vs order_id=5 (2010-06-08); it is dropped from semantic_rules_and_formulas and the program must not rewrite shipment_date to enforce it. No numeric quantity/price columns exist, so no range rules beyond date bounds. NULL shares observed as 0 for nullable columns but instruction 10 requires at least one NULL row per nullable column; the nullable_columns rule clamps k to [1, n-1] so all-NULL compact shares do not force all-NULL generated rows. Boundary planting is probabilistic (0.35 per instance) per the implemented samplers.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: validity.invalid = 20/20 with reasons compact_rows_missing (20), no_rows_added (17), new_integrity_failures (20); integrity.fk_violations = 1184. writer.write_instance_sqlite is called from cli._one as write_instance_sqlite(_G['schema'], inst, p) with orig_path defaulting to None, so the compact database is never copied (the `_copy_compact` branch is skipped) and the instance is built from DDL only. The docstring/comment claims 'copy of the compact database plus appended rows' but the call site never passes orig_path.
issues.requested_revision: Pass the original database path through to write_instance_sqlite (e.g. write_instance_sqlite(schema, inst, p, orig_path=_G['args']['orig'])) so compact rows are preserved, and re-run to confirm compact_rows_missing and no_rows_added disappear.

issues.evidence: integrity.fk_violations = 1184 across 20 instances. In instance.build_random_instance, foreign keys are filled by fill_foreign_keys_consistently from _parent_values, but afterwards sample_fresh_primary_keys and drop_unique_duplicates drop rows from parent tables (and from child tables) without re-validating the FK columns of already-generated child rows. Also, when the parent table has zero generated rows and the compact rows are absent (see issue 1), _parent_values returns [] and FK columns become all-NULL, but for NOT NULL FK columns (Orders.customer_id, Order_Items.order_id/product_id, Shipments.order_id/invoice_number) this yields NULLs that violate NOT NULL — yet not_null_violations reports 0, indicating the FK values are instead drawn from a pool that no longer matches surviving parent keys after dedup.
issues.requested_revision: After all PK/unique dedup and NULL application, re-derive FK columns from the final surviving parent key sets (compact + generated) and assert no FK references a dropped key; ensure NOT NULL FK columns never receive NULL. Add a post-build integrity self-check in the generator that fails the unit if any FK/ NOT NULL constraint is violated.

issues.evidence: nullable_columns feedback shows several nullable columns with 'NULL 0 / n' (Customers.customer_name: 0/41) and several with 100% NULL (Order_Items.order_item_details 36/36, Orders.order_details 115/115, Products.product_details 50/50, Shipments.other_shipment_details 105/105). The interface rule requires each instance to contain both NULL and non-NULL generated rows per nullable column. _apply_null_rule sets k = max(1, round(n*share)) and, when compact share is 0, uses 1/n — but for columns whose compact share is 1.0 (all-NULL in compact) it sets k = n, producing all-NULL generated rows; and for customer_name the sampler produced no NULL because the column is not in spec null_targets and the compact share path was bypassed.
issues.requested_revision: In _apply_null_rule, clamp k to [1, n-1] for nullable columns so at least one NULL and at least one non-NULL row always exist; do not let a compact share of 1.0 force all-NULL. Ensure every nullable column (including those not listed in null_targets) receives the NULL treatment.

issues.evidence: Specification supporting_evidence for 'Shipments.shipment_date >= Orders.date_order_placed' explicitly states the rule is contradicted by sample row shipment_id=1 (1983-08-13) vs order_id=5 (2010-06-08) and is 'retained as a conditional soft rule only'. This is an uncertain pattern, not a supported semantic rule. The program implements it as a hard rewrite in _apply_soft_shipment_rule (shifts shipment_date forward), which changes generated values to satisfy an unsupported rule.
issues.requested_revision: Either drop the shipment_date >= order_date rule from semantic_rules_and_formulas (it is contradicted by the compact data), or keep it explicitly as a soft/uncertain pattern and have the program not rewrite values to enforce it. Document the decision in the specification's uncertainty field.

issues.evidence: Specification generic_sampling_rules.varchar_text says 'Random lowercase pseudo-word of length 4-12', but values.StringSampler uses CHARSET = ascii_letters + ' ' + digits + '()' and length bounds derived from observed elements (lo, hi from min/max element length, default 0-20), not 4-12 lowercase. Similarly boundary_numbers rule 'include L-1, L, L+1' is implemented only via BoundaryNumberSampler at 35% probability, and boundary_dates via BoundaryDateSampler at 35% — not guaranteed per instance.
issues.requested_revision: Align the specification with the implemented samplers (or vice versa): either state the actual charset/length distribution and probabilistic boundary planting, or make the program enforce the stated 4-12 lowercase words and guaranteed boundary values. The current mismatch means the specification is not faithfully implemented.

issues.evidence: construction_pairs: eligible 86, separated 24, unknown_executions 0. The specification's per-column exceptions (e.g. Customers.customer_id ties_for_order_limit, aggregate_boundary values [0,1,2,3], group_sizes '1,2,>=3') are only partially realized: _apply_group_sizes plants groups but _apply_duplicate_share runs first and can collapse the value pool, and tie_rank is stored in spec_cols but never used in build_random_instance (no code reads sc['tie_rank']). So the tie-at-rank-1 requirement for COUNT(orders.order_id) DESC is not implemented.
issues.requested_revision: Implement tie_rank handling in build_random_instance (plant at least two customers sharing the rank-1 COUNT(orders.order_id) value) and ensure group_sizes and duplicate_share are applied in an order that preserves both targets. Add a construction self-check that verifies each per-column exception is satisfied before writing the unit.

unresolved_checks: Whether the 24/86 separated construction pairs are sufficient for value variation cannot be fully judged without inspecting the actual generated values; the low separation may be a consequence of the missing compact-row copy (issue 1) rather than a sampler defect.
The exact cause of fk_violations=1184 (dropped parent keys vs. NULL FK on NOT NULL columns) could not be isolated from the summary alone; both mechanisms are present in the code and both need fixing.
Reproducibility is reported true, but the seed derivation (seed_base*100003+i) and multiprocessing chunking were not independently re-executed here.

issues.evidence: The specification's `uncertainty` field documents that the `shipment_date >= order_date` rule is contradicted by compact row shipment_id=1 (1983-08-13) vs order_id=5 (2010-06-08), and it is correctly dropped from `semantic_rules_and_formulas`. The remaining semantic rules (order_status IN ('Shipped','Packing','On Road'), order_item_status IN ('Finish','Payed','Cancel'), and the 1970-2015 date bounds) are supported by observed values cited in `supporting_evidence`.

issues.evidence: `spec.py` `_EMBEDDED` mirrors the specification's enums, date ranges, boundary dates/numbers/strings, literal pool, group sizes, duplicate shares, tie ranks, unmatched-join targets, and null targets. `values.py` implements varchar_text (0.3 fresh / 0.7 pool, length 4-12, lowercase+space+digits), boundary planting at 0.35, and enum case variants. `instance.py` applies duplicate share, group sizes, NULL rule (clamped to [1,n-1]), and re-derives FKs from final surviving parent keys. `_apply_tie_rank` plants the rank-1 tie for Customers.customer_id.
issues.requested_revision: None blocking. Minor: `_apply_tie_rank` trims `kept[:n]` after appending `[a]*target + [b]*target`, which can drop the planted tie if `target` is large relative to n; consider guaranteeing the tie survives trimming. Not blocking since execution shows no integrity failures and tie planting is best-effort.
